description: Capture payment-fraud incidents with bank-account objects and fraud-focused galaxies/taxonomies so analysts can correlate mule accounts, recipients, channels, and social-engineering patterns across a financial sharing community.
name: Financial fraud case

structure.help: Start with the operational facts your peers need for de-duplication and rapid triage in shared financial communities.
structure.label: Case overview

structure.help: Your internal case number or ticket id. Keep it stable; it is used in the default event title.
structure.label: Case reference

structure.help: Short description such as APP scam, invoice fraud, card-not-present refund fraud, business email compromise payout, or account takeover cash-out.
structure.label: Fraud type summary

structure.help: When the fraudulent activity was first observed by your team (ISO 8601).
structure.label: First seen

structure.help: Free text is intentional (for example: `USD 24,500 attempted / USD 6,000 settled`).
structure.label: Attempted/actual loss amount

structure.help: Add the transaction, channel, and beneficiary indicators that enable cross-institution correlation.
structure.label: Payment and channel indicators

structure.help: Reference id provided by core banking, PSP, card processor, or Faster Payments rail.
structure.label: Transaction reference

structure.help: Examples: SWIFT, SEPA, FPS, ACH, RTP, card transfer, crypto off-ramp.
structure.label: Payment rail

structure.help: Name as supplied in the payment order or onboarding artifacts.
structure.label: Beneficiary/account holder name

structure.help: Phone number used by the fraudster (social engineering call-back, mule onboarding, payment redirection).
structure.label: Fraud contact phone

structure.help: Email address used in scam communications or payout instructions.
structure.label: Fraud contact email

structure.help: URL for fake KYC pages, scam landing pages, or redirection portals tied to the fraud flow.
structure.label: Fraud portal / payment URL

structure.help: Use the dedicated bank-account MISP object so account identifiers and routing details are normalized for correlation. Add one object per recipient/mule account.
structure.label: Bank account objects

structure.help: Recipient or mule account linked to the fraud case. Use + Add another instance for each additional account.
structure.label: Suspicious bank account

relations.help_override: Full IBAN when available (most useful field for cross-community correlation).
Local account number if IBAN is unavailable.
Beneficiary name tied to this account.
ISO currency used for transfers into this account.

structure.help: Attach artifacts that peers can use for verification, retro-hunting, and regulatory reporting workflows.
structure.label: Evidence and enrichment

structure.help: Upload remittance slips, screenshots, or payment confirmations (redact customer PII where required).
structure.label: Payment proof or statement

structure.help: One or two lines with context that will help partners decide whether to freeze, reject, or monitor linked payments.
structure.label: Analyst note

structure.help: Map the case to fraud-specific galaxies/taxonomies so downstream communities can query by modus operandi and framework coverage.
structure.label: Fraud classification and intelligence context

structure.help: Choose the sharing color that matches legal/privacy constraints for this case.
structure.label: TLP

structure.help: Select the ATT&CK4Fraud cluster(s) that describe the fraudster behavior in this case.
structure.label: ATT&CK4Fraud technique

structure.help: Map the case to the MITRE Fight Fraud Framework cluster(s) used by your community.
structure.label: MITRE Fight Fraud Framework

structure.help: Choose Taxonomy of Fraud cluster(s) to normalize fraud scenario naming across institutions.
structure.label: Taxonomy of Fraud

structure.help: Optional cross-reference to law-enforcement, FIU, or consortium identifiers.
structure.label: External partner case id

structure.content: **Sharing note:** include at least one normalized bank-account object and one fraud framework mapping (ATT&CK4Fraud, MITRE Fight Fraud Framework, or Taxonomy of Fraud) whenever possible. This sharply improves cross-organization correlation and speeds up preventive controls.
